records.evidence: 2026 conference abstract O33: ENERGIZE open-label extension NCT04770753 had 182 entrants; 121 were originally mitapivat-treated. Among 55 primary responders, mean reported hemoglobin-response duration increased from 17.9 weeks in double-blind treatment to 43.6 weeks including extension. Of 121 continuing mitapivat, 72 (59.5%) showed an open-label Hb response. Open-label post-hoc, subject to selection and no contemporaneous randomized control; not independent replication.
records.criticalLimit: Exploratory post-hoc OLE; durability observation is not independent randomized confirmation.

records.evidence: ENERGIZE-T trial NCT04770779: treatment emergent AEs 155/172 (90%) mitapivat and 71/85 (84%) placebo; serious AEs 19/172 (11%) versus 13/85 (15%); ten (6%) vs one (1%) discontinued study treatment for adverse events. Open-label long-term safety remains ongoing.
records.criticalLimit: Reported 48-week randomized safety denominators; does not prove longer term safety or FDA benefit-risk acceptance.

records.evidence: 48-week double-blind ENERGIZE-T treatment discontinuations due to adverse events were 10/172 (6%) mitapivat versus 1/85 (1%) placebo; no deaths reported. OLE endpoints pending.
records.criticalLimit: Duration 48 weeks; adverse-event causality and longer term risk not independently settled.

records.evidence: EMBARQ-CSU1 randomized Phase 3 barzolvolimab efficacy at 150 mg Q4W persisted through Week24: UAS7=0 complete response 42.4% at Week12 and 49.0% at Week24 versus placebo 9.3% and 15.4%, with sponsor-adjusted p<0.00001. Separate study CSU2 corroborates primary efficacy but long-term Week52 is not yet available.
records.criticalLimit: Issuer-filed topline; full 52-week durability and complete SAP/missing-data assessment not established.

records.evidence: EMBARQ-CSU2 randomized Phase 3 barzolvolimab 150 mg Q4W had Week12 UAS7=0 response 45.7% and Week24 54.0% versus placebo 12.6% and 17.6% (sponsor-adjusted p<0.00001). Separate CSU1 corroborates the Week12 endpoint; 52-week outcomes remain pending.
records.criticalLimit: Issuer-filed topline, not independently reanalyzed complete long-term datasets.

records.evidence: EMBARQ-CSU1 omalizumab-refractory subgroup Week12 UAS7=0: 150 mg Q4W barzolvolimab 55.3% versus 9.3% placebo, company-reported p<0.00001. No confirmed interaction p-value, subgroup multiplicity, or independent review.
records.criticalLimit: Subgroup observation, not proof of effect modification.

records.evidence: EMBARQ-CSU2 omalizumab-refractory subgroup Week12 UAS7=0: 150 mg Q4W 41.7% vs placebo 15.1%, issuer p=0.0089. Detailed interaction tests and multiplicity strategy unavailable.
records.criticalLimit: Prespecified subgroup status not independently established; not head-to-head with omalizumab.

records.evidence: Celldex 2026 Q3 SEC filing describes barzolvolimab as well tolerated to Week24 in EMBARQ-CSU1. Phase3 exact-study arm-level serious AE and discontinuation tables are not provided by this qualitative statement.
records.criticalLimit: Qualitative issuer safety characterization only; do not assign post-1-5 grade based solely on this.

records.evidence: Celldex 2026 Q3 SEC filing describes barzolvolimab as well tolerated to Week24 in EMBARQ-CSU2. No full exact-study arm-level severe events/discontinuation table is established by this statement.
records.criticalLimit: Qualitative sponsor description insufficient to grade post-1-5.

records.evidence: IZAR-1 trial NCT06641076 sponsor reports improvements in HAQ-DI and SF-36 PCS with sonelokimab in biologic-naïve psoriatic arthritis. Magnitudes, confidence intervals, and full independent comparison were not in the cited topline description.
records.criticalLimit: No arm-level numerical patient-reported effect size verified; not a new numerical grade.

records.evidence: MoonLake's IZAR-1 press release states blinded safety consistent with previous studies and no new safety signals. It does not provide complete matched serious-event and discontinuation tables for the studied dose.
records.criticalLimit: Qualitative source fact, insufficient to grade post-1-5 safety.

records.evidence: ABTECT-Maintenance NCT05535946: Week-44 clinical remission rates 50.8% (25 mg, 98/193) and 51.3% (50 mg, 100/195) versus placebo 10.4% (20/192), both comparisons p<0.0001.
records.criticalLimit: Sponsor topline; not a prospective prediction or complete FDA-grade trial review.

records.evidence: Sponsor reports endoscopic improvement 54.9% and 64.1% for 25 and 50 mg versus 12.5% placebo at Week 44.
records.criticalLimit: Secondary results require multiplicity, missing-data and patient-important benefit review.

records.evidence: Sponsor reports no new safety signals among 580 participants in the Week-44 maintenance trial.
records.criticalLimit: Qualitative safety statement without complete matched adverse-event tables does not justify numerical safety grade.

records.evidence: ENERGIZE NCT04770753 randomized Phase 3: hemoglobin response 55/130 (42%) mitapivat vs 1/64 (2%) placebo, adjusted difference 41 percentage points (95% CI 32–50), p<0.0001.
records.criticalLimit: Non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia trial; not separate ENERGIZE-T; no approval inferred.

records.evidence: ENERGIZE adverse events in 107/129 (83%) mitapivat versus 50/63 (79%) placebo; headache 22% versus 10%, initial insomnia 14% versus 5%; no deaths.
records.criticalLimit: Complete severity and longer-term safety review needed.

records.evidence: ENERGIZE-T transfusion reduction 52/171 (30%) mitapivat versus 11/87 (13%) placebo; adjusted difference 18 points (95% CI 8–27), p=0.0003.
records.criticalLimit: Randomized 48-week result in transfusion-dependent adults; open-label extension is separate.

records.evidence: RISE UP NCT05031780 had mixed co-primary outcomes: hemoglobin response 56/138 (41%) vs 2/69 (3%), p<0.0001; annualized pain crises 2.6 vs 3.1, p=0.1213.
records.criticalLimit: Pain-crisis co-primary did NOT reach significance; do not label the overall program an unqualified success.

records.evidence: RISE UP serious adverse events 28/138 (20%) mitapivat versus 20/69 (29%) placebo; one and zero respectively judged treatment related.
records.criticalLimit: SAE rates alone are not a complete benefit-risk score.

records.evidence: ACTIVATE-KidsT primary transfusion reduction was 28.1% mitapivat vs 11.8% placebo but prespecified Bayesian criterion not met with low/moderate adult-data borrowing.
records.criticalLimit: Trial did not satisfy prespecified primary statistical criterion; descriptive response advantage alone does not reverse that.

records.evidence: ACTIVATE-Kids NCT05175105 enrolled 30 children, 19 mitapivat and 11 placebo; sponsor reports primary hemoglobin endpoint met under Bayesian analyses using adult-data borrowing.
records.criticalLimit: Small pediatric sample and borrowed adult information need explicit uncertainty assessment.

records.evidence: LUCIDITY NCT06747468 randomized 78 participants; avexitide reduced Level 2/3 hypoglycemic event rate 55% relative to placebo, p=0.000003.
records.criticalLimit: Sponsor topline; absolute event counts, confidence intervals, detailed SAP not yet independently adjudicated.

records.evidence: Sponsor reports most events mild/moderate, no drug-related SAEs; diarrhea and injection-site reactions among common adverse events.
records.criticalLimit: No published matched severity/withdrawal table in cited announcement; numerical safety rating not automatic.

records.evidence: Pediatric APeX-P berotralstat interim n=29: no drug-related Grade 3/4 or serious AEs, deaths, or AE-related discontinuations reported.
records.criticalLimit: Small uncontrolled interim population; not a definitive long-term safety comparison.

records.evidence: APeX-P reported pediatric PK median Tmax 3.9 hours, geometric mean Cmax 204 ng/mL and AUC0-last 915 ng·h/mL.
records.criticalLimit: Observed drug exposure is not randomized demonstration of efficacy; primary PK endpoints may be non-binary.

records.evidence: COMP006 (crosswalked to NCT05711940) reported Week-6 MADRS mean difference -3.8 points for two 25-mg COMP360 doses vs 1-mg comparator (95% CI -5.8 to -1.8), p<0.001.
records.criticalLimit: Company report; comparator 1 mg not placebo, and crosswalk established by COMP006 registry study ID.

records.evidence: COMP006 sponsor report: six treatment-emergent SAEs in six 25-mg participants (2%); most TEAEs dosing-day, most resolved within one day.
records.criticalLimit: Sponsor-reported safety; psychiatric and suicidality risks require careful full-population interpretation.

records.evidence: FDA ROSELLA trial efficacy: PFS hazard ratio 0.70 (95% CI 0.54–0.91), median 6.5 vs 5.5 months, p=0.0076; OS hazard ratio 0.65 (95% CI 0.51–0.83), median 16.0 vs 11.9 months, p=0.0004.
records.criticalLimit: FDA report confirms realized dual primary survival outcomes, not future prediction.

records.evidence: FDA approved relacorilant with nab-paclitaxel on March 25, 2026 based on ROSELLA NCT05257408 and other submitted evidence.
records.criticalLimit: Specific FDA drug/indication approval is distinct from another trial’s approval or future forecast.

records.evidence: ACACIA-HCM Phase 3: KCCQ-CSS Week 36 difference 3.0 points (95% CI 0.5–5.5), p=0.02; peak oxygen uptake difference 0.67 mL/kg/min (95% CI 0.22–1.11), p=0.003.
records.criticalLimit: Dual primary outcomes; magnitude of patient benefit must be assessed beyond statistical significance.

records.evidence: ACACIA-HCM LVEF reductions to under 50% in 27/258 (10.5%) aficamten versus 2/259 (0.8%) placebo; serious AEs 52/258 (20.2%) versus 38/259 (14.7%).
records.criticalLimit: Important safety counterweight to efficacy; do not infer absence of cardiomyopathy risk.

records.evidence: IMerge Phase 3: at least 8-week RBC transfusion independence 47/118 (40%) on imetelstat versus 9/60 (15%) placebo (difference 25 points), p=0.0008.
records.criticalLimit: Randomized trial includes subsequent extension/substudies; distinct phases must not be pooled.

records.evidence: IMerge grade 3-4 TEAEs 107/118 (91%) imetelstat vs 28/59 (47%) placebo; neutropenia 68% vs 3%, thrombocytopenia 62% vs 8%.
records.criticalLimit: High hematologic toxicity burden must be explicitly evaluated despite primary efficacy success.

records.evidence: FUSION NCT04768972: sponsor reports primary joint rank of survival, rescue and ALSFRS-R change to day 505 statistically significant for ulefnersen versus placebo (p=0.0005).
records.criticalLimit: Complex composite primary; full component effects, subgroup confidence intervals and sensitivity analyses needed before numerical clinical rating.

records.evidence: FUSION sponsor describes most adverse events as mild or moderate and treatment as favorably tolerated.
records.criticalLimit: No full arm-level AE/SAE and discontinuation table is available in this topline description; safety grade remains missing.

records.evidence: FDA cites randomized NCT04849741 with 49 patients age 2 and older supporting zilganersen: improved walking speed at 61 weeks among assessable participants aged at least five, and improvement on pediatric gross-motor scales among ages 2–4.
records.criticalLimit: The age groups use different clinical endpoints; youngest under-2 efficacy relies on pharmacokinetic extrapolation, not concurrent randomized efficacy.

records.evidence: FDA lists vomiting, back pain, cough, headache and post-lumbar-puncture syndrome as common side effects and notes aseptic meningitis risk.
records.criticalLimit: FDA label warning should be evaluated; no generic safety success based solely on approval.

records.evidence: FDA approved Zanvastro (zilganersen) for Alexander disease on September 3, 2026, with NCT04849741 among supporting studies.
records.criticalLimit: Confirmed current FDA regulatory outcome, not an FDA approval probability for another drug.

records.evidence: OASISplus NCT05392114 extension: 83 patients received donidalorsen Q4W or Q8W; 75/83 (90.4%) completed year one. Mean attack rates fell 94% and 95% from parent OASIS-HAE baseline under open-label extension.
records.criticalLimit: Open-label continuation and selected rollover participants are not independent randomized replication; parent trial NCT differs.

records.evidence: At one-year OASISplus, 22/83 (27%) patients reported treatment-related adverse events; none serious; injection-site reactions most frequent.
records.criticalLimit: Open-label extension; cannot infer placebo-controlled long-term comparative risk.

records.evidence: VERIFY NCT05210790: 113/147 (77%) rusfertide versus 48/146 (33%) placebo achieved no-phlebotomy-eligibility clinical response in weeks 20–32, p<0.0001.
records.criticalLimit: Current randomized result; interpret composite response definition and intercurrent events before assigning research rating.

records.evidence: VERIFY patient-relevant effects: mean phlebotomies 0.5 versus 1.8 over double-blind observation; hematocrit below 45% in 63% versus 14%; PROMIS fatigue improved vs placebo (p=0.0252).
records.criticalLimit: These are secondary endpoints and patient-reported outcomes; active treatment and background care context matter.

records.evidence: VERIFY publication describes fixed-sequence multiplicity control across primary/key secondaries; delta-adjusted multiple imputation sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness.
records.criticalLimit: Published design and sensitivity narrative are evidence, but numerical score requires verifying the exact prespecified model, missingness and clinical effect thresholds.

records.evidence: TRANSCEND NCT05774756 randomized 120 participants: at Week 52 least-squares BMI change -16.5% with setmelanotide vs +3.3% placebo, p<0.001.
records.criticalLimit: BMI change is observed; age-mixed groups and clinical risks must be considered for benefit rating.

records.evidence: TRANSCEND hunger score change -2.73 setmelanotide vs -1.45 placebo, p=0.009, in eligible participants at least 12 years old.
records.criticalLimit: Patient-reported symptom benefit differs by age and subgroup; clinical meaningfulness must be assessed.

records.evidence: TRANSCEND any adverse events 100% on setmelanotide vs 90% placebo; serious adverse events 28% vs 8%, with skin hyperpigmentation, nausea, vomiting and headache commonly reported.
records.criticalLimit: Safety imbalance should count in overall research assessment; not automatically outweighed by positive BMI endpoint.

records.evidence: IMPALA-2 NCT04544293: sponsor reports statistically significant Week-24 DLCO percent predicted improvement for inhaled molgramostim versus placebo, sustained at Week 48.
records.criticalLimit: Issuer topline does not substitute for the precise adjusted between-arm effect estimate, confidence interval and SAP.

records.evidence: IMPALA-2 sponsor reports significant Week-24 St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire total score and nominally significant activity and treadmill exercise outcomes.
records.criticalLimit: Patient-reported and functional outcomes must be distinguished from nominal secondary p-values and controlled multiplicity.

records.evidence: ENVISION NCT05243550 single-arm Phase 3 in recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC: at three months 191/240 (80%; 95% CI 74–85) achieved complete response to UGN-102.
records.criticalLimit: Single-arm design; do not attribute randomized superiority or mix this study with controlled ATLAS.

records.evidence: Among ENVISION 3-month complete responders, estimated probability of remaining event-free 24 months after CR was 72% (95% CI 64–79).
records.criticalLimit: Responder-only time-to-event estimate with loss to follow-up and selection; not a controlled durability comparison.

records.evidence: ORIGIN3 prespecified interim NCT04716231: 203 patients; Week-36 proteinuria reduction 45.7% atacicept vs 6.8% placebo, geometric mean between-arm difference 41.8 percentage points (95% CI 28.9–52.3), p<0.001.
records.criticalLimit: Prespecified interim surrogate proteinuria result; final kidney function and clinical outcome data remain separate.

records.evidence: ORIGIN3 interim adverse events reported in 59.3% atacicept versus 50.0% placebo; most mild/moderate.
records.criticalLimit: Interim safety observation does not establish all long-term infection and renal outcomes; no numerical safety grade inferred.

records.evidence: ABTECT-Maintenance 580 participants, placebo/25mg/50mg: any TEAE 50.0%/58.0%/71.8%; serious TEAE 4.2%/2.6%/5.6%; treatment discontinuation due to AE 6.8%/2.6%/4.6%; deaths zero in all arms.
records.criticalLimit: Issuer SEC exhibit; dose-dependent TEAE frequency and rare cancers require complete adjudicated safety report. No automatic FDA risk verdict.

records.evidence: Reported adjusted placebo contrasts for Week-44 primary remission used Mantel-Haenszel weights across stratification factors including baseline remission, induction dose and oral corticosteroid use; both active doses p<0.0001.
records.criticalLimit: Complete SAP, confidence intervals, full missing-data sensitivity and multiplicity review were not included in this SEC summary.

records.evidence: ABTECT-1 and ABTECT-2 are distinct Phase 3 randomized induction studies with 50mg Week-8 clinical remission versus placebo 21.7% vs 2.5% (ABTECT-1) and 19.8% vs 6.3% (ABTECT-2), significant in both; 25mg did not meet the primary in ABTECT-2 (11.3% vs 6.3%, p=0.1034).
records.criticalLimit: Induction populations and Week-8 endpoint differ from BOTTOM maintenance Week-44 randomized responder-trial design; not independent maintenance replication.

records.evidence: Week-44 endoscopic remission (placebo/25mg/50mg) 9.9%/41.5%/47.7%, histologic-endoscopic improvement (HEMI) 10.4%/50.3%/57.4%, corticosteroid-free remission 9.9%/45.1%/47.7%, reported p<0.0001.
records.criticalLimit: Complete hierarchy, multiplicity and independent patient-level validation are not available from this topline filing alone.

records.evidence: Reported placebo-adjusted Week-44 remission effect of obefazimod 25mg was +39.3 percentage points and 50mg +40.3 points, clinical remission 50.8% and 51.3% versus 10.4% placebo.
records.criticalLimit: Source is company SEC-hosted summary; no standalone, independent final CSR or full confidence interval for both differences established.

records.evidence: Drug discontinuations due to treatment-emergent adverse events in the 44-week randomized maintenance trial: placebo 13/192 (6.8%), 25mg 5/193 (2.6%), 50mg 9/195 (4.6%).
records.criticalLimit: Treatment-discontinuation-from-AE is not complete trial attrition or all-cause missingness; full disposition and imputation remain unreviewed.

records.evidence: After two Phase 3 induction trials, 580 clinical responders were randomized to 25mg obefazimod (n193), 50mg (n195) or placebo (n192) for 44-week maintenance; original source identifies placebo and responder re-randomization.
records.criticalLimit: The maintenance placebo is a withdrawal/re-randomization control among responders, not an unselected UC population or head-to-head active-drug comparison.

records.evidence: 580 previously induction-responsive ulcerative-colitis participants were re-randomized in ABTECT-Maintenance to placebo n192, obefazimod 25mg n193, 50mg n195; stratification adjusted remission at baseline, induction treatment and baseline oral corticosteroid use.
records.criticalLimit: Reported group sizes and stratification do not alone prove prospective power assumptions, final SAP adequacy or missing-data robustness.

records.evidence: Final ROSELLA trial 24.8-month median follow-up overall survival 16.0 months combination versus 11.9 months control, HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51-0.83), p=0.0004.
records.criticalLimit: Observed survival is important to patients; symptom and QoL scores require independent assessment.

records.evidence: FDA approval for ROSELLA cited serious safety warnings for neutropenia/severe infection, adrenal insufficiency and steroid contraindication.
records.criticalLimit: Regulatory approval does not imply no adverse events.

records.evidence: FDA summarized randomized BICR PFS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.54-0.91), p=0.0076 and OS HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51-0.83), p=0.0004.
records.criticalLimit: Detailed multiplicity and missing-data sensitivity not fully in short FDA summary.

records.evidence: Final Lancet ROSELLA OS HR 0.65 was consistent with prior interim analysis HR 0.69 after longer follow-up.
records.criticalLimit: These analyses use one trial; not independent replication.

records.evidence: Mature ROSELLA randomized observed overall survival extended by 4.1 median months versus active monotherapy control.
records.criticalLimit: No prospective prediction or generalization outside the trial's population.

records.evidence: ENERGIZE-T NCT04770779 used a 48-week randomized blinded period and a primary transfusion response defined in any consecutive 12-week interval. Its extension is open-label and planned up to five years. The 48-week endpoint is not proof each patient maintained response across 48 weeks.
records.criticalLimit: Ongoing extension is not independent placebo-controlled replication; long-term individual response durability cannot be inferred from primary 12-week response window.
